name: Executive order of September 1, 1887 setting apart the Uintah military reservation at Fort Duchesne
aka: Fort Duchesne military reservation executive order, 1887
nations: Ute Indian Tribe of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation
promises: Not a treaty: an executive order. Royce records that the President set apart as the Uintah military reservation a tract around Fort Duchesne, Utah Territory, 2 miles wide and 3 miles long, beginning 2 miles due north of the fort's flagstaff.
today: Royce places the tract inside the Uintah reservation (area 431). The Uintah Valley Reservation was confirmed by Congress in 1864; the Indian Claims Commission (Docket 45, 1957) said that in every instance where reservation land was taken compensation was paid. No court, claims-commission, Act of Congress or government finding about this military reserve was found, in the Commission's full text ('Fort Duchesne' appears only as a meeting place) or in the Court of Claims case list.

openQuestions: Whether the military reservation was later returned to the tribe, and on what terms, was not researched. A 1960 Commission record describes Fort Duchesne as the location of the Uintah and Ouray Indian Agency, but how the land came back was not traced.
treaties.json gives Royce area 431; Royce marks this entry 'See 431' and says the rectangular tract is outlined in scarlet. Not edited.
treaties.json lists no present-day tribes; the Ute Indian Tribe of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation should be listed. Not edited. The executive order link (431r.pdf) was not opened.

Audit 2026-11-08: Royce p. 924 order text read: rectangle 2 miles wide by 3 long from a point 2 miles due north of the Fort Du Chesne flagstaff, matching the promise. Docket 45 opinion (id 86) re-read for the 'in every instance ... compensation was paid' statement. No finding found: ICC full text 'fort duchesne' returns only settlement-meeting records (ids 428, 710); all 14 Ute and Uintah Court of Claims cases from ctcl-index searched for 'military reserv', 'Fort Duchesne', 'Du Chesne' with no hit. No-breach-found confirmed.
